solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crashing a car and losing horn?

indicators.note: a car that is crashing gets smashed up, so the letters that follow are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver crashes and, in the wreck, the car's horn stops working.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'horn' looks like the car's hooter, but it is a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind instrument also known as the English horn, a member of the oboe family.

clue.text: Embroider cover protecting piano

indicators.note: something protecting another thing wraps around it, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: an overlay is a covering laid over something
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A needleworker stitches a decorative cover to shield a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embroider' looks like sewing, but here it means exaggerating a story or performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider a tale is to exaggerate it, and to overplay something is likewise to overstate or overdo it.

clue.text: Old king drops charioteer's gift

indicators.note: a king who drops something lets it fall away, so those letters leave his name

blocks.note: the legendary King Arthur of Camelot
the charioteer Ben-Hur is literally son of Hur, so what is the charioteer's is Hur

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch lets slip a present given by a chariot racer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur is the chariot-racing hero of the novel and film; 'Ben' means son of, so the charioteer's name supplies HUR to strip from ARTHUR, leaving ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift in the sense of a natural talent or knack is an art, as in having the art of persuasion.

clue.text: Carp is good and ready to eat …

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
fruit that is ready to eat is ripe

explanation.surface: A cook declares the carp in good condition and ready for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish, especially with the next clue about fish, but it is the verb for complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily, and to gripe is to grumble in the same way: a verb synonym.

clue.text: … fish with beer on it is initially extremely flavoursome

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters of the next word count

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
W is a common abbreviation for with
the opening letter of this word
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Continuing from the carp, a fish served with beer poured over it tastes wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, beer 'on' with sits above it, so ALE comes first; 'it' is just W.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American fish of the herring family, so it is a specific example of a fish.

clue.text: Toady law enforcer joins in shanty at sea

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the word next to it is scrambled
someone who joins in goes inside a group, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: a cop is a police officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A policeman joins the crew singing a sea shanty on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A toady flatters people in power for advantage, which is exactly what a sycophant does: a noun synonym.

clue.text: Furtively look towards the left and right

indicators.note: reading towards the left and towards the right gives the same word, so it reads identically both ways

blocks.note: a quick glance, and the same four letters whichever way they are read

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks glances to the left and then to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in either direction, which is what looking left and right hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to glance quickly and secretly, as through a keyhole, so it is a furtive kind of look.

clue.text: A firm kiss with Tory about to make one colour

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Co is the abbreviation for company
a peck is a quick kiss
blue is the Conservative Party's colour, so a Tory is a blue

explanation.surface: A company's office romance with a Conservative politician produces something colourful.
explanation.walkthrough: The kiss goes about A CO, then the Tory follows. Blue for a Conservative comes from the party's campaign colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacock blue is a named shade, the greenish-blue of a peacock's neck feathers, so it is one particular colour.

clue.text: It's not odd to follow the Spanish cardinal

indicators.note: one thing set to follow another comes after it, fixing the order of the pieces

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
a number that is not odd is even

explanation.surface: Apparently it is perfectly normal to defer to a Spanish cardinal of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it means a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers, one, two, three and so on, and eleven is one of them.

clue.text: Live with a flash girl

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
in a trice means in a flash, an instant

explanation.surface: Someone moves in with a flashy young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A trice is a moment, so 'a flash' gives A TRICE; 'with' just joins it on.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice is a female first name, and crosswords often define any given name simply as girl.

clue.text: Mean-spirited Conservative party at end of election

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that last letter is taken

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a rave is a lively party
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A sour Tory celebrates once the votes are counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Craven means cowardly and contemptible, a sense of mean-spirited as lacking courage or nobility of spirit.

clue.text: After medical procedure I had such?

definitions.text: After medical procedure I had such?

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: an op is an operation
taken as written
to have a meal is to eat, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: A patient recalls being given a painkiller after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: after an op, a patient might well be given a painkiller of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a drug derived from opium, such as morphine, typically given for pain relief after surgery.

clue.text: When out with armourer Pope endlessly shows self-respect

indicators.note: endlessly means without an end, so the last letter is cut off
letters that are out are disordered and put back in a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: On a night out with a weapon-maker, the pontiff still keeps his dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour propre is a French phrase used in English for self-esteem, a sense of one's own worth.

clue.text: One politician strolls after rallies

indicators.note: after places what precedes it behind what follows it, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
to rove is to wander or stroll

explanation.surface: A lone politician wanders about following political rallies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rallies' looks like a noun for political meetings, but it is the verb for recovering.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient or market that rallies recovers and gets better, so the verb is a synonym of improves.

clue.text: Show of praise received when choking?

blocks.note: first meaning: a gesture of congratulation
second meaning, taken literally: what someone gets when food goes down the wrong way

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: someone choking gets a literal slap between the shoulder blades.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative pat on the back is a gesture of congratulation, while a literal one is the thump given to a choking person.

clue.text: Bird on the stove, in a container still

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so it comes first
in places the preceding pieces inside the following one

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird
an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker, the classic farmhouse stove
a tin is a metal container

explanation.surface: A chicken sits on top of the kitchen range, inside a pot that is not moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adjective for not moving, but it is the adverb meaning nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, used as a sentence adverb meaning however or nevertheless, is matched by the phrase then again.

clue.text: There's some white in this paint

definitions.text: There's some white in this paint

blocks.clueFragment: There's some white in this paint
blocks.note: surface reading: a tin of paint mixed with a little white pigment
setter's reading: the casing that once held an egg's white, and also the name of a matt paint finish

explanation.walkthrough: The white is egg white, not pigment; the answer is both the casing round it and a low-sheen paint finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a paint finish with a slight sheen, named for resembling the surface of an egg's casing, which encloses the white.

clue.text: Love meal laced with yoghurt – it's a hospital's speciality

indicators.note: something laced with another thing is mixed through it, so these letters are blended together

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital's signature dish turns out to be a lovely meal with yoghurt stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speciality' suggests a house dish, but it means a medical specialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatology, the study and treatment of joint and connective-tissue disease, is a hospital department or medical specialism.

clue.text: Short girl has to get slip

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a miss is a girl or young woman
to take is to get or obtain

explanation.surface: A little girl must go and fetch her petticoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like an undergarment, but it means an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error or oversight, so it is a synonym for a mistake.

clue.text: Talk aggressively about the French excursion

blocks.note: le is French for the
a trip is an excursion or outing

explanation.surface: Someone rants angrily about a French outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an idiom for speaking out without restraint, especially angrily, so it means to talk aggressively about something.

clue.text: Rating ham and pork, say, without carnivores

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so one piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: erk is slang for a low-ranking sailor or airman, a rating
ham and pork are examples of meats

explanation.surface: A sailor turns down the ham and pork, refusing to be a meat-eater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' looks like assessing, but it is a naval rank, and 'without' means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Meerkats are small African mongooses, members of the mammal order Carnivora, so they are carnivores in the zoological sense.

clue.text: It's said to make you smile

definitions.text: It's said to make you smile

blocks.clueFragment: It's said to make you smile
blocks.note: surface reading: something said to be a mood lifter, like a joke
setter's reading: the word a photographer gets you to say aloud so your mouth forms a grin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' means literally spoken: photographers ask sitters to pronounce this word because it shapes the lips into a grin.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying this dairy word for the camera is a traditional trick to produce a smile in a photograph.

clue.text: Trophy I had for archer

blocks.note: a cup is a sporting trophy
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A competitor claims to have won a prize for archery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid, the Roman god of love, is pictured with bow and arrows, so he is the archer of mythology.

clue.text: Doctor entertains artist with piano and a brandy

indicators.note: a host who entertains takes guests in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a GP is a general practitioner
RA is a Royal Academician
p is the musical abbreviation for piano
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor hosts a painter who plays the piano, and pours a brandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian spirit distilled from grape pomace, so it is a kind of brandy.

clue.text: Made false allegations about a new press journo

indicators.note: something new has been remade, so the following word is reformed into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
ed is short for editor, a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A fresh reporter from the papers smeared someone with lies.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to cast aspersions on them, attacking their reputation with damaging, often false, accusations.

clue.text: Atkinson, say, loses an argument

indicators.note: a name that loses something has those letters taken out of it

blocks.note: Rowan Atkinson is the English comic actor of Mr Bean
taken as written, the letters to be removed

explanation.surface: The comedian Rowan Atkinson comes off worse in a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Atkinson is an example of someone called Rowan, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a noisy quarrel, so it is a synonym of argument.

clue.text: Some despair about part of church

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the answer is a run of letters inside the next word
about means turned round, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A churchgoer feels a little despair about one area of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess, usually at the east end, of a church, so it is one part of the building.

clue.text: Stupidly we enrolled useless oaf

indicators.note: doing something stupidly makes a mess of it, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone regrets foolishly signing up a lazy idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A ne'er-do-well is a lazy, good-for-nothing person, so a useless oaf is a fair description.
